content:
Noah Patel: trying to close the loop on the design question from triage: when we detect “stuck TP group” (no forward progress / collective timeout / async error), do we (a) quarantine the TP group and keep the host alive, or (b) restart the whole host/pod immediately? Need to be explicit about failure domain + correctness.

Sofia Ivanova: +1. scheduler perspective: quarantine is cheaper, but only if we can guarantee we don’t schedule onto a potentially corrupted execution context.

Hiro Tanaka: from kernels/collectives: once NCCL throws (or we hit `ncclCommAbort`), you basically can’t trust the communicator. You can *sometimes* recreate comms, but if the process is wedged in CUDA land it might not come back. So “quarantine + controlled teardown of ranks” seems safer than “keep limping”.

Sean Gallagher: SRE angle: host restart is a big hammer. If we restart nodes too aggressively we’ll amplify impact during load (especially Dedicated). Prefer smallest blast radius: quarantine the TP group (stop taking traffic), then attempt graceful teardown; only reboot host if repeated.

Rafael Mendes: agree w/ Sean, but we need clear semantics: quarantine means: stop new work *immediately*, drain or cancel in-flight, and publish a signal so router/scheduler doesn’t keep sending.

Grace Kim: correctness concern: if one rank lags and we cancel, we can land in barrier deadlock. if we “unstick” by force-canceling streams, could we ever return partial tokens that are wrong? my worry is after comm failure, KV cache contents across ranks might diverge.

Noah Patel: yep. I think rule should be: any collective error / timeout => request fails closed. i.e. return 5xx and do not attempt to continue generation on that group.

Allison Grant: +1 “fail closed”. if we keep returning tokens from a half-broken group, debugging becomes impossible and customers see silent quality corruption.

Sofia Ivanova: if we do quarantine at TP-group level, we need to define exactly what state is scoped to the group vs shared on the host. Current runtime has per-rank worker processes w/ multiple TP groups per host (depending on packing). A host-level restart is too wide if only 1 group is bad.

Hiro Tanaka: note: NCCL communicators are per process and often reused across groups. depending on our mapping, an abort may poison more than one TP group if they share ranks.

Isabella Rossi: what are we calling “TP group” here? exact tuple of ranks participating in TP for a model instance? If so, group == set of GPU processes. If we’re doing one process per GPU, then group spans N processes. So if group is bad, probably need to restart those N processes anyway.

Noah Patel: good call. We should align definitions:
- failure domain A: TP group (set of ranks participating in one TP instance)
- failure domain B: host (node)
- failure domain C: pool/zone
I’m leaning: primary mitigation = quarantine TP group, then restart only the worker processes in that group (not whole node) if possible.

Tomáš Novák: from oncall/runbook: we need a deterministic playbook. If watchdog triggers, what should oncall see? “TP_GROUP_QUARANTINED” + “TP_GROUP_RESET_ATTEMPTED” + “TP_GROUP_RESET_FAILED => HOST_DRAIN”.

Rafael Mendes: +1. Also, need to guard against a flapping group (false positive). e.g. if group is just slow (long seq) we don’t want to quarantine. So watchdog should be “no progress” not “slow progress”.

Sofia Ivanova: scheduler can give you “progress” in terms of tokens emitted per rank. we can track per-rank step counters and require no increment for X sec.

Grace Kim: what’s “progress” if request is blocked in an all-reduce before producing next token? It’ll look like no token output. we need a lower-level signal too (e.g. collective start/end timestamps) otherwise we’ll quarantine healthy groups under high load.

Hiro Tanaka: yes. in kernels we can bracket collectives w/ NVTX + structured logs. We can record last successful collective completion timestamp. Watchdog uses that, not token output.

Sean Gallagher: ok but then correctness: if we see collective latency spike (slow but not stuck), we should alert not quarantine. quarantine should only be for “stuck” signature. Strong distinction please.

Noah Patel: proposal:
1) “Stuck” definition (quarantine trigger):
   - no collective completion for > T_stuck AND
   - at least one in-flight request assigned to group AND
   - NCCL async error check reports error OR CUDA event hasn’t advanced (we can use stream progress marker).
2) Quarantine behavior:
   - scheduler marks group HEALTH=QUARANTINED
   - router stops assigning new requests
   - all in-flight requests get canceled and fail closed (explicit error code)
3) Recovery attempt:
   - controlled teardown: abort communicators, tear down rank workers in group, recreate group
   - if recreate fails or repeats N times in M minutes => drain host.
Thoughts?

Allison Grant: logging/telemetry should include reason codes (e.g. `reason=NCCl_ASYNC_ERR`, `reason=NO_PROGRESS`, `reason=WATCHDOG_FALSE_POSITIVE_OVERRIDE` etc). Otherwise dashboards will be unusable.

Rafael Mendes: need to be careful with “abort communicators” inside a live process: if a rank is hung in a kernel, abort call might itself hang. We should set a hard timeout and then kill -9 the worker. Container runtime handles cleanup.

Hiro Tanaka: +1. I would not rely on “graceful” if CUDA is wedged. Policy: attempt `ncclCommAbort` + `cudaDeviceSynchronize` with timeout; if not returning in e.g. 2s, hard kill the process. (We can debate exact numbers.)

Sofia Ivanova: scheduler can initiate group reset by signaling the supervisor (per-host agent) to restart only those ranks. But if ranks share a process supervising multiple GPUs, we might restart too much. Current deployment is 1 proc per GPU, so OK.

Isabella Rossi: perf consideration: if we restart N procs, we lose warmed KV cache and possibly model weights residency (depending on how we load). That could cause tail latency spikes. Better than total outage, but we should expect a small spike and document.

Sean Gallagher: for Hosted pools, that’s acceptable if we keep it rare and we have enough headroom. For Dedicated, we need opt-in + clear comms. Also, if you’re restarting processes, you’re effectively doing a mini blackhole: we should make sure the routing layer sees reduced capacity immediately.

Connor O'Brien: release side: please don’t add “host reboot” as default behavior in 1.19 without a feature flag. If we mis-tune, we can thrash.

Noah Patel: yes. feature flag around quarantine + reset, and separate flag for “host drain on repeated failures”.

Grace Kim: correctness Q: do we ever attempt to migrate an in-flight request from a quarantined group to another group? like resume generation from last token?

Sofia Ivanova: not safely today. we don’t persist per-request KV cache/state in a way that can migrate across TP groups. best we can do is retry from scratch at app layer if idempotent.

Noah Patel: agreed: no mid-flight migration. We fail the request and rely on client retry. For streaming, make sure we terminate stream with explicit error so clients don’t hang.

Tomáš Novák: can we standardize the error code/message? Oncall needs to identify in logs quickly. Something like `TP_GROUP_UNHEALTHY` and `COLLECTIVE_STALL_DETECTED`.

Allison Grant: yes and add a unique incident key for correlation: `tp_group_id`, `host_id`, `model`, `build_sha`.

Rafael Mendes: also, boundary question: if we see repeated stalls across *all* TP groups on same host, that’s likely host-level GPU/driver issue. That’s where host drain/reboot is warranted. single group => group reset.

Hiro Tanaka: +1. that’s the “failure-domain boundary” we should write down: group-level errors are recoverable; host-level systemic errors require drain.

Sean Gallagher: can we codify “systemic”? ex: >K groups quarantined on same host in <10 min => drain host. Or if GPU X has repeated Xid errors.

Noah Patel: sounds good. I’ll write in ADR language:
- Default action: quarantine TP group + restart group ranks.
- Escalate to host drain when: repeated group resets, multi-group correlation, GPU health signals.

redwood-incident-bot: Reminder: Action items from Sev1 follow-up include: define quarantine semantics, document runbook, add dashboards. Linked incident: https://confluence.redwood/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=sev1-tp-hang-2025-02-13

Sofia Ivanova: ok but let’s ensure scheduler state machine has a “RESETTING” state so we don’t race (e.g. new work assigned while ranks are restarting).

Grace Kim: and cancellation semantics must ensure we don’t block on barriers while canceling. (this is the deadlock bug we’ve seen.)

Noah Patel: yep. I’ll pull Sofia/Hiro into a quick doc update. Tentative decision in thread: quarantine + group-rank restart as primary, host drain only on escalation; fail closed for correctness; no in-flight migration.

Sean Gallagher: :thumbsup: Please include explicit guardrails/thresholds + feature flags in the design so SRE can roll out safely.

Connor O'Brien: :thumbsup: when you have a draft, tag me so I can align with hotfix/patch policy.

Allison Grant: :thumbsup: and ping me for the reason-code taxonomy so dashboards aren’t a mess.

Noah Patel: will do.
